title: Spiral traversal
summary: Walk a matrix in a spiral and generate one, using four shrinking boundaries.
hints: Keep four boundaries: `top := 0`, `bottom := rows - 1`, `left := 0`, `right := cols - 1`. Loop while `top <= bottom && left <= right`. Each pass walks the outer ring - top row left to right, then right column top to bottom, then bottom row right to left, then left column bottom to top - and after each side moves that boundary inward (`top++`, `right--`, ...).

The classic bug: after the first two sides you must re-check `top <= bottom` before walking the bottom row, and `left <= right` before walking the left column. Otherwise a matrix with a single row or column gets some cells visited twice.

`SpiralMatrix(n)` uses the very same walk, but instead of reading `m[r][c]` you *write* an incrementing counter: allocate the `n x n` matrix, keep `next := 1`, and assign `m[r][c] = next; next++` in each of the four loops.
